reconcile.note: Matthew Henry reads Proverbs' earthly recompense as partial, not final, so the incompleteness of temporal justice points forward to the fuller reckoning at the last judgment.

discrepancy.note: Voltaire presses that the Mosaic law grounded justice in this life alone, crediting the New Testament, not Proverbs' wisdom, with revealing an afterlife of reward and punishment.

quotes.text: The greatest benefit we owe to the New Testament is that it has revealed to us the immortality of the soul. … One should bless the revelation of the immortality of the soul, and of rewards and punishments after death, all the more that mankind's vain philosophy has always been sceptical of it.
quotes.attr: Voltaire (d. 1778), A Philosophical Dictionary (1764), "Of the Need of Revelation," on Proverbs 11:31 and Revelation 20:12.

sides.snippet: the righteous shall be repaid in the earth; How much more the wicked and the sinner!
sides.verseText: Behold, the righteous shall be repaid in the earth; How much more the wicked and the sinner!

sides.snippet: The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works.
sides.verseText: I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and they opened books. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged out of the things which were written in the books, according to their works.
